sections.h2: Which selling routes make sense in Waukegan?
sections.html:
Listing with an agent, selling without one and taking a cash buyer's as-is bid are all open to a Waukegan owner. The city paperwork is the same for all three, so the choice mostly turns on how much repair work, waiting and showing you want to take on.

Waukegan faces Lake Michigan, roughly 11 miles below the Wisconsin line and 37 miles up the shore from downtown Chicago, and no other Lake County city has more people. The 2020 census counted 89,321, and the estimate for mid-2025 stands at 87,940. With roughly 32,000 households, the city has a large local housing market, and it adds a transfer step that many Illinois towns do not have, covered next.

sections.h2: What is the Waukegan zoning certificate and closing letter?
sections.html:
Every change of ownership in Waukegan needs a zoning certificate, a life-safety inspection and a closing letter. The city's Closing Letter / Zoning Certificate page says the rule took effect October 16, 2023, under Ordinance 23-0-294.

The online application is due at listing, and in any case at least 30 days ahead of closing. A code officer calls within five days of the fee payment to book a minimal code and life-safety inspection. The certificate has to hang where it is fully visible, as near the front entrance as possible, for the whole time the home is on the market.

The city's FAQ is blunt about exceptions: its ordinance lists none, so foreclosure and tax-sale transfers need the same documents. Each parcel number in a sale needs its own closing letter, and a missing number can hold up the closing.

  • Seller side: property details, occupancy status, number of bedrooms or units, MLS number if listed, and the listing agent's contact information.
  • Buyer side, once you have one: a driver's license number for the water account transfer, receipts for any city amounts already settled, and a notarized affidavit.
  • Utility side: call the Water Department at least five business days before closing to schedule the final meter reading (847-360-0535).

The closing letter is issued only after the fees and the final water bill are paid. Any liens on the property are disclosed in the record, and the payoff statements can be settled at closing.

sections.h2: Is an as-is sale allowed in Waukegan?
sections.html:
Yes, with conditions. The city's FAQ allows an as-is sale when the zoning certificate inspection is done and the buyer signs a notarized affidavit. The city does not provide a template, so the affidavit has to carry a date, the buyer's address, phone number and email, a list of the items the buyer takes on from the inspection report, the buyer's signature and the notary's confirmation.

That matters for a fast sale. A cash buyer who agrees to take the inspection items does not hold the closing up for repairs, though the inspection itself still has to happen. Sellers who wait until a contract is signed to apply risk running into the 30-day window.

State law adds a separate duty: residential sellers give the buyer a completed disclosure report before signing (765 ILCS 77/20). Transfers from an estate fiduciary, by court order or in lieu of foreclosure are among the exempt ones listed in Section 15.

sections.h2: What do Waukegan homes and households look like on paper?
sections.html:
Five-year survey results show a city split almost evenly between owners and renters, with values well under those in suburbs to the south.

  • Owners occupy 50.2% of homes
  • Middle value among owned homes: $190,900
  • Middle monthly rent including utilities: $1,205
  • 32,042 households of about 2.72 people
  • Midpoint household income $71,919; 15.3% of residents in poverty
  • Bachelor's degree or above, adults 25 and up: 20.9%

The city's roots are industrial. Its harbor, a railroad through town by 1855 and later plants such as a sugar refinery and a barbed-wire maker drew workers from Sweden, Finland, Lithuania and elsewhere. The 2023 annual financial report lists Lake County, Southwire, Vista Medical Center East, Lake Behavioral Hospital and Medline Industries among the largest employers. The city has also pursued a lakefront plan to replace much of the old industrial shoreline with residential and recreational space.

sections.h2: What do Waukegan schools, roads and transit mean for a listing?
sections.html:
Most of Waukegan belongs to Waukegan Community Unit School District 60, which serves about 17,000 students from preschool through grade 12. Waukegan High School runs on two campuses, Brookside for grades 9 and 10 and Washington for grades 11 and 12. Pieces of the city fall inside Gurnee School District 56 with Warren Township High School District 121, and a small section sits in Beach Park District 3 and Zion-Benton District 126, so look at the district named on the tax bill before you describe schools in a listing.

Buyers who commute will look at the Metra Union Pacific North line, the Pace bus hub at Sheridan Road and Washington Street, the Tri-State Tollway and the Amstutz Expressway. The Robert McClory Bike Path crosses the city, and Waukegan National Airport handles general aviation. The lake also tempers the climate, cooling summers and warming winters.

sections.h2: What if the Waukegan house is a rental?
sections.html:
According to the city's rental license page, every rental inside city limits needs a license before anyone moves in. Licenses expire each December 31, the fee is $60 per rented unit, and an application needs planning and zoning pre-approval plus a passed inspection by the Building and Code Department. A code officer reaches out within five business days to schedule it.

Where tenants occupy the house, keep the license current while it is listed and tell prospective buyers about the lease early. Ask the city's License Department how the license is handled when ownership changes.

sections.h2: Who records a Waukegan deed, and what goes on it?
sections.html:
Deeds for Waukegan homes are filed in the county building at 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, with the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office (phone 847-377-2575). Its fee schedule lists a $70 standard document fee and an $82 non-standard fee, and says the only other charges at recording are state and county transfer taxes.

The county's deed packet lists what must be on the document.

  • Signed and dated by the grantor, with a notary acknowledgment
  • The buyer's address, a full legal description and the preparer's name and address
  • A "mail to" address and the name and address for tax bills
  • A completed PTAX-203 declaration or a signed exemption statement

The state tax follows 35 ILCS 200/31-10, which prints the rate as 50¢ per $500 of the value stated in the declaration, counting any fraction of $500. The same packet names six Lake County municipalities that require a local stamp before recording. Waukegan is not on that list, though the closing letter described above applies.

faqs.q: Must a Waukegan seller repair every item the inspector lists?
faqs.a: No. The city allows an as-is sale if the buyer signs a notarized affidavit accepting the listed items. The inspection still has to be done and the certificate issued, so apply as soon as the house is listed or under agreement.

faqs.q: What does the Waukegan closing letter process cost?
faqs.a: The city lists $300 at submittal, split into a $150 zoning certificate fee and a $150 closing letter fee. Any other invoiced amounts owed to the city, including the final water bill, are settled before the letter is issued.

faqs.q: Do foreclosure and tax-sale transfers in Waukegan skip the certificate?
faqs.a: No. The city's FAQ says its ordinance lists no exemptions for transfers such as foreclosure or tax sale, so those transfers also need the application, inspection and closing letter.

faqs.q: Who files the deed after a Waukegan closing?
faqs.a: The Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office takes it, at 18 N County Street in Waukegan. Bring it in or send it by mail; the office phone is 847-377-2575.

faqs.q: How soon can a Waukegan cash sale close?
faqs.a: The city's steps set the minimum: apply at listing, at least 30 days before closing, with an inspector calling within five business days. An as-is buyer can follow that schedule, and title work sets the rest.
